newsitem.title: USA: Baltimore Gas opposes Labor Board decision.
newsitem.headline: Baltimore Gas opposes Labor Board decision.

text.p: Baltimore Gas and Electric Co (BGE) said on Friday it opposes the decision of the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) that only about 2,700 employees of BGE will be able to vote in the upcoming union election.
"This deprives nearly 1,800 employees of a say in whether BGE is unionized," the company said in a statement.
The company said the announcement was the latest event in an organizing effort launched by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW) in Spring 1995.
BGE chief executive Chris Poindexter said in a statement that "our position is that we're not anti-union, we're pro BGE."
The company said it intends to file a request to the NLRB for them to review the decision.

George Creel, the company's acting chief operating officer and the person who oversees the company's effort to remain union-free, said, "BGE has a tradition of excellence that is hard to match in our industry. I attribute that to the fact that our employees can satisfy customers' needs without the kind of restrictive work rules that are typical in IBEW contracts."
